name: certificate-transparency
description: Looks each domain you add to the targets up in the Certificate Transparency logs, through both crt.sh and ctlogs.dev, and merges what the two know: every host name the domain's TLS certificates cover, with its issuers and validity, in the Entity Explorer, and the names on those certificates outside the domain (related domains) under Targets → Related. It sends the target's domain name to crt.sh and api.ctlogs.dev, third-party services.

settings.label: Include expired certificates
settings.description: Off: only certificates valid now. On: expired ones too, which can name hosts long gone (or forgotten but still up). crt.sh then returns the domain's whole history, which for a large domain is a big, slow answer; ctlogs.dev's free tier goes back 90 days past expiry.

settings.label: Certificates to read in full, per domain
settings.description: Neither search lists every name on a certificate, so finding related domains means fetching certificates one by one: the most recent with names not yet seen, one request each. 0 skips it, and lists only the names under the target's domain.

settings.label: Largest certificate to take related domains from
settings.description: A certificate naming more hosts than this is taken to be shared (a CDN's or a SaaS host's, covering unrelated customers), and the names on it outside the target's domain are not listed.

settings.label: ctlogs.dev pages per domain
settings.description: 100 certificates a page, one request each. Without an API key ctlogs.dev allows 100 requests an hour and 10 pages a query.

settings.label: ctlogs.dev API key (optional)
settings.description: Not needed: without one, requests share ctlogs.dev's keyless pool. A free key from account.ctlogs.dev lifts the 10-page limit. It is kept in reProxy's secrets file and sent only to api.ctlogs.dev.
